issues.legal_issue: A challenged will is valid where the evidence establishes its execution by a testator of sound disposing mind and the circumstances relied on to question it do not undermine that proof.
material_facts: The testatrix was elderly, chronically ill, physically weak, and had difficulty writing; evidence showed her hand was trembling and she was unable to sign her name when the will was executed.
The attesting witness and the beneficiary gave evidence that the testatrix was of sound mind and understood what she was doing when she executed the will; the court found their evidence trustworthy.
The court found that the testatrix’s letters showed distress about the challengers’ lack of attention, rather than that the beneficiary had confined or controlled her.
The beneficiary had cared for the testatrix for several years and handled her financial affairs; she had also held a joint bank account and locker with him.
The testatrix died on the day the will was executed, and the will bore her thumb-mark; it was registered after her death and made a general bequest without describing particular property.
issues.conclusion: The will was duly executed and valid, and the appeals challenging it were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the alleged suspicious circumstances against the evidence of execution and testamentary capacity. It treated the testatrix’s physical inability to sign as consistent with her thumb-mark, while finding that she had a sound disposing mind. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case.

rule.if: will_validity_appeal and testator_sound_mind and physically_unable_to_sign and execution_witnesses_credible and (alleged_control_unsupported or beneficiary_had_prior_trust_and_care)

predicates.will_validity_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity or due execution of a will.
predicates.testator_sound_mind: The testator understood what they were doing when the will was executed.
predicates.physically_unable_to_sign: The testator was physically unable to sign their name when the will was executed.
predicates.execution_witnesses_credible: The court found credible the evidence of witnesses to the will’s execution.
predicates.alleged_control_unsupported: The evidence did not support the allegation that the beneficiary controlled or confined the testator.
predicates.beneficiary_had_prior_trust_and_care: The testator had previously trusted the beneficiary with personal care or financial affairs.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a will, and the testator was of sound mind but physically unable to sign, credible execution evidence supports the will, and the alleged control is unsupported or the beneficiary had an established relationship of trust and care, the will is upheld.
